extracted.intended_audience: researchers in psychology, cognitive science, anthropology, and scientifically-minded readers interested in mental imagery/memory
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical description and collection of cases of 'Number-Forms' (vivid spatial mental images of numerals), including methods for eliciting, verifying, classifying, and measuring them. The page reports prevalence, family heredity, stimulus influences, and examples with plates/diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity and independent confirmation of reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The answers I received whenever I have pushed my questions, have been straightforward and precise. I have not unfrequently procured a second sketch of the Form even after more than two years' interval, and found it to agree closely with the first one. I cannot doubt of the authenticity of independent statements which closely confirm one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek independent confirmations, request repeated sketches separated by long intervals, compare verbal and written reports across correspondents, present examples at scientific meetings so multiple knowledgeable witnesses can corroborate (author brought several gentlemen whose diagrams were suspended on the walls). Use the internal evidences in a large mass of correspondence to judge trustworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational definition of a Number-Form
rubrics_metrics.description: It consists in the sudden and automatic appearance of a vivid and invariable 'Form' in the mental field of view, whenever a numeral is thought of, in which each numeral has its own definite place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record what kind of Form (line, row(s) of figures, shaded space), whether each numeral has a stable position, and whether the appearance is sudden/automatic and invariable. Note whether Arabic numerals are seen, whether the Form is 'in' a background or 'in front', and whether persons or ages occupy specific places.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevalence reporting and sampling transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: The peculiarity in question is found, speaking very roughly, in about 1 out of every 30 adult males or 15 females. School returns showed about one in twenty (18 of 337) boys had well-defined Number-Forms; personal inquiries among adults gave about 1 in 30 as a provisional result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report total returns, ages, and source populations; state denominators and numerators; note whether special groups (masters) should be omitted; account for non-responders, shyness, and possible exaggeration. Present both adult and child/youth samples separately and discuss selection biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early origin and persistence over time
rubrics_metrics.description: These forms originate at an early age; they are subsequently often developed in boyhood and youth... Nearly all of my correspondents speak with confidence of their Forms having been in existence as far back as they recollect. One states that he knows he possessed it at the age of four.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask about earliest recollection, school learning (e.g., multiplication table), and follow-up after years to confirm persistence. Use parents/teachers to test children and repeat inquiries after intervals to document continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vividness, utility, and developmental strengthening vs neglect
rubrics_metrics.description: If they are too faint to be of service they are gradually neglected, and become wholly forgotten; while if they are vivid and useful, they increase in vividness and definition by the effect of habitual use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish faint/ineffective forms from vivid/functional ones; record whether the subject uses the Form as a mnemonic (e.g., to learn tables). Track changes in vividness over time and correlate with habitual use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence for heredity (familial occurrence)
rubrics_metrics.description: I have the strongest evidence of its hereditary character after allowing, and over-allowing, for all conceivable influences of education and family tradition. I have no less than twenty-two families in which this curious tendency is hereditary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect pedigrees/case series in families, look for extension beyond parent/child to siblings and further degrees, compare shapes of Forms within families (similarity of shape is evidence), and explicitly consider and try to rule out shared environmental/educational explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence of external artifacts and linguistic nomenclature
rubrics_metrics.description: Children learn their figures to some extent by those on the clock... The other traces of the origin of the Forms... are dominoes, cards, counters, an abacus, the fingers... But the paramount influence proceeds from the names of the numerals... Three quarters of the Forms bear a duodecimal impress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record any identifiable external source (clock-face, domino spots, tools, local geography, nursery rhymes) and linguistic naming conventions that create systematic distortions (e.g., hitches at 12 and 120). Pay attention to how numeral names (verbal system) conflict with decimal notation and leave characteristic scars in Forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spatial, geometric and qualitative attributes to record
rubrics_metrics.description: About one-third of the figures are curved to the left, two-thirds to the right; they run more often upward than downward. They do not commonly lie in a single plane. Sometimes a Form has twists as well as bends... It is often sloped upwards at a slight inclination from a little below the level of the eye.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When documenting a case, record direction (left/right), slope (upward/downward), curvature, 3D orientation and perspective difficulties, presence of twists, whether parts are brighter/dimmer, and relative positions (e.g., where 1, 100, 999 lie). Use drawings, woodcuts, and, where possible, stereoscopic/photo models to capture perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colour, shading and segmental definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Forms are sometimes variously coloured, occasionally very brilliantly... In all of these the definition and illumination vary much in different parts... Up to 30 I see the numbers in clear white; to 40 in gray; 40-50 in flaming orange; 50-60 in green; 60-70 in dark blue...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note colours and shading for number ranges, record which zones are more distinct, and whether colour changes correspond to numerical divisions. Use coloured plates/illustrations to preserve reports; ask subjects to comment on possible exaggeration from thinking it over.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal/processing measurements (timing and quantification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments were made as to the time required to get these images well in the mental view... twenty numbers of two figures each... gone through in 22, 16, and 26 seconds... general result of 23 seconds for twenty numbers, or 2-1/3 seconds per number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use timed trials to quantify visualization speed, repeat trials to get averages, include mixed-digit series for ecological validity, and report variance across trials. Attempt measurements of scale (space occupied by numbers) but report negative results if hypotheses (e.g., geometric diminution) are not supported by averaged measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguishing genuine imagery from voluntary imagination/reporting artefact
rubrics_metrics.description: There was a little difficulty in the performance, because it is only by catching oneself at unawares, so to speak, that one is quite sure that what one sees is not affected by temporary imagination... My great fear has been that in thinking it over I might be led to write down something more than what I actually see.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elicit spontaneous responses, use casual/unexpected questioning to avoid rehearsal, request sketches drawn without prolonged reflection, and obtain repeated blind checks (e.g., delayed re-elicitation) to ensure the image is stable and not constructed after the fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification, presentation and exemplar documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: I give woodcuts of representative specimens of these Forms, and very brief descriptions of them extracted from the letters of my correspondents. Sixty-three other diagrams on a smaller scale will be found in Plates I., II. and III., and two more which are coloured are given in Plate IV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide illustrative plates/figures with accompanying quotes/explanations, group examples by source (schoolboys, adults, families), highlight exemplary or elaborate cases in full-page reproductions, and include both verbal descriptions and diagrams for completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for a 'good' or well-defined Number-Form case
rubrics_metrics.description: The hereditary tendency is on the whole the strongest in those cases where the Number-Forms are the most defined and elaborate... the number of these that contained well-defined Number-Forms are 5, 1, and 12 respectively... I need only describe Fig. 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider a case 'well-defined' if the subject can provide a consistent sketch, if the Form is elaborated (distinct positions, shading, colours), if it serves mnemonic functions, and if it is reproducible over time and corroborated by independent questioning. Use such cases as principal exemplars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence for sudden developmental changes or new stages
rubrics_metrics.description: This is the only case known to me of a new stage in the development of a Number-Form being suddenly attained... 'The growth of 80 was sudden, and has remained constant ever since.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor cases longitudinally to detect abrupt changes in form (new salient numbers or reorganization), document timing and subject commentary on onset, and report rarity of such sudden stage changes while treating them as noteworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to personal idiosyncrasy (handwriting, search patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Handwriting is greatly modified by the fashion of the time... I am sure, too, that I can trace a connection between the general look of the handwritings of my various correspondents and the lines of their Forms... different persons had decided idiosyncracies [in search patterns].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare number-form geometries with subjects' handwriting and habitual visual/search behaviours; gather complementary behavioural observations (e.g., how they search for lost objects) to support links between idiosyncratic motor/visual preferences and mental-form geometry.
